FOREWORD
' the

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by Shipbuilding Sectional Committee had been approved by the Transport Engineering Division, Council. This standard has been prepared to give recommendations and requirements for fuel oil piping, system of ships' main engine with the object of uniformity and proper working of the system. In preparing this standard due consideration practices regarding the use of ferrous materials. has been given to factors involved and currenb

Attention shall be given to the design, fabrication and installation of systems to ensure streamlined' flow. In particular, abrupt changes in the direction of flow, mismatched pipe bores, tube bore protrusions and other restrictions to flow shall be avoided. At each stage of construction it is the responsibility of the user of this Indian Standard to ensure compliance with the requirements of the statutory authoritier and/or classification society as. applicable. Y'he Committee responsible for the preparation of this standard is given in Annex A.

specifies requirements for the materials, design, installation, inspection and testing of fuel oil piping system of ships' main engine including all fittings which form part of such system. 1.2 For the purpose of this standard, the fuel oil piping system includes all pipes and fittings from the oil tanks to pump suction and the oil return ,pipes from engines to the tanks and engine inlet but excludes all heat exchangers. 2 REFERENCES The following Indian Standards -adjuncts to this standard: IS No. `812: 1957 2712 : 1979 -3233 : 1965

3.1 Design Pressure 4.1 The

the following

The maximum pressure to which the system may ,be subjected when in service and is the value used in design calculations. This pressure may result from a combination of circumstances unlikely to occur under normal working conditions. But it shall not be less than the highest set pressure of the safety valve or relief valve, if provided.
3.2 Test Pressure

engine builders recommend a dual pressure system for high viscosity fuel of 500 cSt/SO"C and above. Fuels having such viscosities require to be heated to a temperature as high as 130�C. There is possibility of fuel oil vapourising at this temperature at the suction of the main engine fuel pumps causing vapour lock failure to inject fuel. For this reason the fuel oil is fed to the main engine pumps in two stages by means of low pressure ( primary ) and high pressure ( secondary ) booster pumps. A typical fuel oil diagram for slow speed engines depicting the arrangement is given in Fig. 1. 4.2 In all other cases, a single pressure system consisting of one set of pumps to deliver the fuel to the main engine fuel pumps is used. 5 BLENDING
5.1 General

The pressure to which the system and its components are subjected under test conditions.
3.3 Piping System

All pipes, pumps, valves and fittings and piping from the oil tanks to the pump suction and the oil return pipes from engines to the tanks exclu.ding all heat exchangers.

Diesel engine fuels include a variety of petroleum products ranging from gas oil to heavy fuel oil. Gas oil is produced from crude oil by distillation and processing, whereas fuel oil is mainly the residue left after distillation of the crude oil.

IS 14140 : 1994 -5.2 Heavy fuel is usually a blend of residual oil with lighter components to achieve a desired viscosity. .5.3 If blending of fuels on board ships is intended, where direct burning of heavy fuel is not `desirable for some medium speed engines, care shall be taken to make sure that the components .selected are compatible. Incompatibility of fuel can cause operating problems such as heavy sludging in the separators, filter plugging and `deposit formation in engine. High viscosity fuel oil is sometimes further blended on board with diesel oil to produce an intermediate viscosity fuel suitable for auxiliary diesel and medium speed engines. The blending equipment, heater, ratio of blentiing. etc, shall be in accordance with the recommendations of the engine builder. ,5.4 Suitable measures shall be taken on starting up and stopping of the engine as well as prolonged idling on heavy fuel oil as per engine manufacturer's operating instructions. 6 PUMPS .&I Type and Selection of Pumps 7 SETTLING/SERVICE ,Fuel oil shall be generally supplied to engine by positive displacement rotary pumps. Selection of the pump shall be based on the inherent advantages of one type over the other. 6.1.1 The pumps shall have in-built safety valve or relief valve which shall be a part of the `system. 6.1.2 Usually two pumps shall be installed, one as stand by, and driven by separate electric The motor rating shall be determined motors. by considering the oil viscosity when starting from cold. q6.2 Capacity of Pumps 6.2.1 Pumps shall be able to deliver the preheated heavy fuel oil or diesel oil to the fuel injection pumps under pressure at a larger flow than required. This prevents malfunction due to the formation of a vacuum and the accumulation of gas vapour in the fuel injection pumps. The capacity and delivery pressure shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and manufacturer in line with the engine builder's recommendation. .6.2.2 The pump capacity may have to be filter increased if an automatic back-flushing using the filtered fuel oil for back-flushing is installed. ~6.3 Mounting of Pumps 6.3.1 Pumps shall be mounted in such a way 7.1 General The relative positioning of tanks to each other with regard to tank levels must be followed. Preferably the shipside shall not be used as a boundary for any such tanks. Similarly, such tanks shall not have a common boundary with any ballast tanks or accommodation deck. The tanks equipment shall comply with the rules of the Classification Societies. The tanks have the following common features: Provision shall be made for drainage of sludge, solid particles and water from the bottom of the tanks. The drain valve or cock shall be self closing type. TANKS that they are readily accessible for maintenance and so arranged that any one pump may be opened up for overhauling/repair while other pump is in operation. 6.3.2 The mounting surface provided for the pump and motor shall be rigid and able to prevent coupling mis-alignment due to work load and temperature variations. 6.3.3 The temperature of the heavy fuel oil at feed pump inlet usually exceeds 100�C: Therefore, to avoid pumping trouble due to the formation of vapour in the suction pipe it is recommended that the booster pump be installed to have flooded suction. Also the resistance to flow in suction line shall bz kept as small as possible. 6.4 Control of Pumps The independently driven pumps are to be capable of being stopped from a position outside the space which shall be always accessible in the event of fire occurring in the compartment in which t,hey are situated as well as from the compartment itself.

b) Drain is to be provided

at the lowest point in the tank. It is essential to design the bottom of the tanks to slope downwards to facilitate collection of sediment and water. the injection system, the outlet pipe shall be positioned so that the fuel shall be drawn off at a level well above the tank bottom.

d) Heating coil shall be provided for all fuel oil tanks. For diesel oil provision of heating is not necessary. Heating of oil in the settling and service tanks shall be limited to 10�C below the Hash point and shall be controlled by a thermostat. Temperature of heating medium shall not exceed 220�C.

g) Deflector shall be fitted near to the filling points to avoid splashing of oil during filling of the tank. h) In general, there shall be two manholes namely, one on the tank wall the lowest point of which shall be about 300 mm from the bottom and another on the top surface of tank; in the case of tanks of less than 5 m3 capacity only one manhole may be provided on top or at a convenient place. j) A thermometer pocket. k) All fuel oil outlet valves shall be of quick closing type with provision for remote and manual operation for oil fuel tanks which are situated above the double bottom tanks, the inlet and outlet pipes, which are connected to the tank at a point lower than the overflow pipe or below the top of the tanks without an overflow pipe, shall be fitted with shutoff valves located on the tank itself. These valves shall be accessible and capable of being closed from positions outside these spaces in the event of fire occurring in these spaces. Where non-return valves are provided in the inlet pipes which are connected below overflow lines, quick closing valves with remote control are not required. Outlet conr.ections of tanks having smaller capacities of 500 litres and less need not be provided with quick closing/ remote control valves. m) All heated tanks with heating provisions shall be suitably insulated. n) A drip tray shall be arranged in way of all fittings on the tank valves from where oil is likely to drip. This drip tray shall be connected to one of the leak-off tanks to collect the oil. 7.2 Settling Tank 7.2.1 H.O. Settling Tank This contains dirty heavy oil. The main purpose of this tank shall be to: a) act as a buffer tank.

The capacity of the tank shall be decided in consultation with the engine manufacturer of main and auxiliary engines and purchaser. 1.2.2 D. 0. Settling Tank The contaminated diesel oil shall be stored in this tank. This settles out any gross water contamination as well as sediments. The tank capacity depends upon the consumption of the main and auxiliary engines, the mode of operation of ship, etc, and shall be determined from case to case. NOTE - For the fuel oil and diesel
oil settling, tanks described in 7.2.1 and 7.2.2 the bottom drains shall lead to an open funnel or hopper using a self closing spring loaded drain valve so that the contents of discharge may be visually examined. The final discharge of these drains.

shall be led to the leak, off tank.

7.3 Daily Tank

7.3.1 H.O. Daily Tank Fuel oil from the settling tank shall be pumped? to the daily tank through a pre-heater and heavy oil separators. The overflow line from daily tank shall be connected to settling tank in order to allow a continuous separation of heavy fuel oil, independent of the actual engine fuel consumption. A non-return valve without manual control preferably flap type shall be provided in the overflow line to prevent accidental discharge of dirty fuel oil into the daily tank. 1.3.2 D.O. Daily Tank The clean diesel oil from oil separators stored in this tank. 7.4 Mixing Tank ( Buffer Tank ) 7.4.1 The purpose of this tank is to equalize the fuel temperature between the hot surplus oil returning from the engine and fuel oil pumps and the oil flowing in from the daily tank. Furthermore, it provides a smooth transition of fuel viscosity and temperature when switching from Diesel Oil to Heavy Oil and vice versa. 7.4.2 Provision shall be made for cleaning the bottom part of the tank. The capacity of the tank shall be determined in consultation with the engine builder. 4 shall be

work for a single stage operation, but in case of a particularly difficult fuel oil, it shall be possible to work both the separators in series as a purifier and clarifier respectively. The clarifier will not only improve the separation results, but it will also act as a safety device in case the purifier is not well adjusted. The effective separator throughput must be in accordance with the maximum consumption of the engine plant plus a safety margin of about 10 to 15 percent. The separators shall be in continuous operation from port to port. 10.3 To maintain a constant flow through the separators, integral or separate positive displacement type pumps operating at constant capacity shall be installed. 11 CONTROL VALVE

$1 Heating coils shall be provided in the heavy `oil tanks for heating the oil to designed temperature conditions in order to maintain in the proper viscosity and flow conditions system. ,8.2 Pre-heaters shall be provided with the The heavy oil and diesel oil separators. separation temperature shall be controlled within f 2�C and a correctly sized steam valve and pre-heater shall help to maintain constant separation temperature. 8.3 To keep the heavy oil temperature steady, steam tracing lines shall be provided along with the fuel 011 line. 8.4 Relief valves are to be fitted on the oil side of the heaters and are to be adjusted to operate at a pressure of 0'35 N/mm" above that of the supply pump relief valves. The discharge from .these valves is to be led to safe positions. 9 FILTRATION 9.1 Filters may retain solid particles to a certain size. In fuel oil system very fine screen filters shall be subjected to frequent clogging and are impossible to clean properly. practically Therefore, filters having not too small a mesh size need be considered.
9.1.1 Suction Filter

A three-way control valve shall be fitted before the mixing tank which controls the changeover from diesel oil to heavy oil and vice versu. It shall be of manually or electrically or pneumatically operated type.

13 DESIGN OF PIPE LINE SYSTEM 13.1 General 13.1.1 In designing a fuel oil system certain configurations and some types of fittings which give an appreciable pressure loss shall be avoided, if possible. 131.2 Pipes used in the system shall comply with required pressure ranges and shall conform to relevant Indian Standards. The type and material of the flexible pipes, bellows and expansion pieces shall be of approved type. 13.1.3 In order to keep pressure losses low, the pipe run shall be as short and direct as possible, tight right-angle bends and T-pieces shall be kept to a minimum. 13.1.4 The diameter of each pipe run shall be determined from considerations of the oil flow quantities and a permissible `maximum velocity-pipe diameter' specification. The length of the pipe shall be such that removal/maintenance is easy. 13.1.5 All pipe lines through which heated oil is flowing shall be insulated along with steam tracing line. 13.1.6 The flexible pipes are to be used only up to the bore size of 50 mm. For bigger sizes
5

The heatable suction filter shall be of the simplex type with a mesh size of about 0'5 to 1'0 mm. The filter shall be fitted before the booster pump. The filter throughput shall be more than 20% of the maximum pump capacity. 9.1.2 Duplex Filter ( Discharge Film ) The heatable duplex filter protects the fuel injection system from damage caused by solid particles. It shall be located as near as possible to the fuel injection pumps. The maximum mesh size shall be 0'05 mm. 10 OIL SEPARATORS down to a certain size. Water and the particles smaller than the mesh size of the filter shall be separated out to a large extent by centrifugal separators. 10.2 The fuel oil from settling tank shall be pumped to the daily tank through a pre-heater and fuel oil separator(s). It is desirable to have at least two fuel oil separators, These shall be installed in the system in such a way that normally each may

13.3.11 Checktng of System On completion of the drawings the system resistance losses shall be re-calculated, the pipe and fitting schedules reviewed and requisitions for equipment confirmed. 13.4 Pressure Loss Through Proprietary Items

The pressure loss through proprietary items may be obtained from the manufacturer's specification. The extra losses to be determined are those occurring in the pipes, valves, bends and other fittings. 14 PIPE WORK FLEXIBILITY AND INSTALLATION 14.1 Flexibility of Piping System SUPPORT

14.1.1 Piping systems shall be designed with adequate flexibility so that expansion of the piping machinery vibration and working of the ship shall not result in over-stressing of the system or leakage at joints. 14.1.2 Flexibility shall normally be provided by the use of plain piping bent to nominal specified radius and offset in the piping. 14.1.3 Where space limitations prevail piping is to be attached to resiliently machinery, use may be made of flexible bellows or expansion pieces. They installed in unstressed condition. or where mounted pipes or shall be

14.1.4 Pipes through which heated fuel oil passes shall be properly insulated along with steam tracing line in order to maintain the temperature steady. 14.1.5 Pressure of fluid in a piping system may result in distortion particularly in way of bends and flexible units if adequate anchorage is not provided. Attention is drawn to the necessity of making such provision as stated in 14.3.3. 14.2 Flexible Piping Units or Assemblies 14.2.1 The design and construction 8 of these

w) Indicate

non-standard joints, materials, fittings, testing procedures, purchaser's special requirements, etc, with drawings.

X) Include essential dimensions

for locating pipe centre lines in the ship where these may be required to produce pipe support fabrication sketches or pipe dimensions.

IS 14140: 1994,

components shall be suitable for the pressure, vacuum and temperature under all conditions likely to occur in service, including ambient and shall also be capable of temperature absorbing the movements imposed by attached machinery and pipe work. 14.2.2 The material of these components including any fittings if separately attached, shall be suitable for containing fuel oil and be compatible with the material of the piping system to which they are attached. 14.2.3 Resistance to damage by fire or other means shall be considered and where deemed necessary a protective arragement shall be given around the flexible components. 14.2.4 Flexible lengths only. pipes shall be limited to small

material shall be pre-cut and so Jointing dimensioned that it will not project into the bore of the pipe. It is recommended that the gaskets be full face and located on the bolts. except where raised face flanges are in use. 14.4.2 Pipe Erection
14.4.2.1 Flange face shall be closely mated and' bolt holes in alignment before making up the joints. The pipes shall not be strained into, position in order to make them fit. Pipes which do not fit satisfactorily shall be retured to the workshop for correction and re-stress relieving. where necessary.

14.4.2.2 Mating pipes, valves and fittings shall; be installed with their bores concentric and in line and care taken to ensure that any jointing fitted does not protrude into the bore. 14.4.2.3 Care shall be taken with alignment of piping when making screwed, brazed or welded joints. 14.4.2.4 The installation of bellow pieces or flexible units shall be carefully carried out to ensure that they are not pre-stressed. 14.4.2.5 The closing length of piping shall be manufactured to a su5cient degree of accuracy. so that it may be fitted in place without undue manual effort. 14.4.2.6 The pipes or any of the fittings in the, system when mounted shall not touch another pipe or fitting or any structural member of the ship. If this is entirely unavoidable, then clamps shall be provided at such points of contact to ensure rigidity of the assembly and to avoid abrasive wear of the material due to vibration and rubbing. 14.4.2.7 Insulation for pipes, where necessary,, shall be provided, only after completing the erection of the line and shall be done such that each length of pipe may be dismantled without cutting the insulation. 15 INSPECTION 15.1 Component Installation AND TESTING Inspections and Tests Before

14.3 Piping Supports 14.3.1 Pipelines shall be routed to enable the surrounding structure to provide logical points of support, anchorage, guidance or restraint. Supporting of the largest of critical piping systems shall take prime consideration over others and the location of supports and anchors shall be shown on arrangement drawings. 14.3.2 The design of supports shall be capable of adequately supporting the piping system without undue distortion. In addition to pipeline gravitational loads, the supports shall provide for concentrated loads imposed by valves and risers, for axial loadings due to expansion and the pressure of fluid, and for inertia effect due to ship movements. Hangers for supports shall be provided close to concentrated weights; as horizontal changes in line direction, and on or adjacent to pipe. 14.3.3 Pipe work adjoining flexible units shall be supported as closely as possible to the flexible unit. The supports shall be designed to prevent the pressure loads transmitted by the flexible unit distorting the attached pipe work and equipment. 14.3.4 The intervals of supports for pipes shall be decided according to the bore and configuration of pipe work. 14.3.5 All pipe work shall be examined during the sea trial to determine whether additional hangers are necessary due to unforeseen vibrations. 14.4 Piping Installation 14.4.1 Pipe Jointing General jointing material shall conform to Grade B/O of IS 2712 : 1979. Other materials between the may be adopted by agreement purchaser and manufacturer.
9

15.1.1 Cleaning of Pipes Pipes shall be internally cleaned and made free from scales. If conditions like corrosive atmosphere exist, pipes shall be suitably protected on the exterior. Where fabricated pipe work is to be used, pipes shall be shot blasted or pickled in random lengths before fabrication. 15.1.2 Shop Inspection 15.1.2.1 All components shall be checked to,

Bureau of Indian Standards

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country.
Copyright

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in &he course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sixes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), BIS.
PReviewof Indian Standards

&nendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicate8 that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the datest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards *Monthly Additions'.
